items.stem: A claims team extracts fixed fields from forms that share one layout. The team must cut model cost and return the same output for the same input. Which design meets the constraint?
options: Read the fixed fields with code rules and skip the model call.
Send each form to Claude Haiku 5.5 at temperature 0, which returns the same output for the same input.
Send each form to Claude Opus 5.5 for field extraction, since the largest tier is the most accurate.
Send each form to Claude Haiku 5.5, where cache hits make repeated field reads free.
items.rationale: Fixed layouts map to fixed outputs, so code rules return the same result with no per-token cost. Only open input needs a model call (Inference).
items.trap: Cache hits look like free reads, but cache hits still cost a small amount per million tokens.

items.stem: A product owner wants summaries that read well. The team must decide whether a model change can ship, and the decision needs a result that passes or fails. Which success criterion meets the constraint?
options: Summaries read well to the support team.
A rating from the model itself looks like a metric, so the team ships when the rating is high.
Summaries score at least 4 out of 5 on a rubric for a fixed test set, signed by the support lead.
Summaries score well on a rubric, reviewed live on a dashboard after release.
items.rationale: A success criterion needs a metric, a threshold, and a named owner (Inference). A rubric score on a fixed test set gives a pass or fail result that the owner can sign.
items.trap: A rating from the model itself looks like a metric, but the same model then grades its own output.

items.stem: A team scores 50,000 nightly support tickets for a report due next morning. Live chat answers must arrive within seconds. The team must keep token cost low for the nightly work. Which two options meet the constraint?
options: Send the live chat through the Message Batches API to lower its token cost.
Send the nightly tickets through the Message Batches API at the batch rate.
Read each nightly result as the model writes it, before the batch ends.
Keep live chat on the synchronous Messages API for answers at once.
items.rationale: Batches cost 50 percent less, and most batches finish within 1 hour, so overnight work fits. Live chat needs answers at once, so it stays on the synchronous API.
items.trap: The batch rate looks like a saving for live chat too. But batch results arrive only when the batch ends, so chat answers would not arrive within seconds.
